# Risk Brief — Compliance & Quality Watch  
**Profile:** Tesla Model Y 2021‑2025; Chevrolet Bolt EV 2019‑2023; Hyundai Ioniq 5 2022‑2025; Volkswagen ID.4 2021‑2025  
**Markets:** EU, UK, US | **Components:** HV battery, airbags, brakes, ADAS cameras/radar, infotainment/OTA  
**Run date:** 2026‑10‑17 | **Open items carried forward:** 86  

---

## Executive summary
- **EU rapid alert (F255)** flags an inverter software fault that can prevent engine restart after EV mode when HV battery charge drops — affects **all four models**; immediate recall/software update action cited.  
- **Tesla Model Y FSD (Supervised) v14.2.2.4** shows a systemic lane‑departure failure mode: 5 complaints in 90 days (2.9× baseline), multiple total‑loss crashes, injuries, fire/smoke, and occupant entrapment; **no recall yet** [S1].  
- **Transport Canada recalls** active for **Hyundai Ioniq 5** (seat/restraint, 2026445) [F265] and **Volkswagen ID.4** (BCM software — power loss/lighting, 2026434) [F269]; verify EU/UK/US scope.  
- **Chevrolet Bolt EV** exhibits three distinct safety‑critical defect trends (door‑latch entrapment, rear‑camera loss, anti‑click washer/brake caliper seizure) with 3 complaints in 90 days each (×3–6 baseline); **no recalls** [S2][S3].  
- **EU regulatory wave**: Delegated Regulation 2026/1753 (battery durability, brake particles, low‑temp range) [F287], V2X 5.9 GHz power limits effective 1 Jul 2025 [F289], and Decision 2025/2234 (UNECE alignment for ADAS/battery) [F275] create near‑term compliance deadlines for Model Y and ID.4.  
- **Supplier risk**: Bosch reports margin erosion and €270M EV‑facility impairments [F299] — monitor component supply continuity.  

---

## Early‑warning signals

| **S2** | Chevrolet Bolt EV — Service brakes (left‑front caliper) | 3 complaints / 90d | 0.49 | Caliper slide‑pin corrosion / anti‑click washer fracture → brake drag, 627°F hub, harness thermal damage, regen‑braking red alert | No | **Serious thermal/mechanical cascade** — tire blowout, brake‑fluid boil, bearing collapse, fire risk; repeat failure post‑repair. |
| **S3** | Chevrolet Bolt EV — Door latch / rear camera / anti‑click washer (drivetrain) | 3 complaints / 90d | 0.99 | Interior release entrapment; persistent rear‑camera loss after repairs; washer fracture locks brake | No | **Three distinct defect trends** masquerading as one spike; each carries serious safety risk (entrapment, blind‑zone backing, loss‑of‑control). |

1. **EU inverter alert (F255)** — obtain OEM root‑cause & fix timeline; confirm software update deployment across all four model fleets.  
2. **Tesla FSD (S1)** — track NHTSA 573.6 filing; monitor OTA hotfix (v14.2.2.4 restriction); request planner telemetry from crash VINs.  
3. **Transport Canada recalls (F265, F269)** — secure VIN‑level applicability for EU/UK/US; initiate regional campaigns if confirmed.  
4. **Bolt EV brake & latch (S2, S3)** — push TSB for caliper slide‑pin; audit dealer repair records for rear‑camera loop; verify 2019‑2020 latch recall coverage extends to 2021‑2023.  
5. **EU regulatory compliance (F287, F289, F275)** — complete battery‑durability/low‑temp test matrix for Model Y & ID.4; validate V2X 5.9 GHz emissions; map UNECE changes to ADAS sensor specs.  
6. **Bosch supplier health (F299)** — request allocation forecast for HV battery BMS ICs, brake‑by‑wire semiconductors, radar MMICs; qualify second sources.  
7. **EU brake‑pedal alert (F270)** — assess pedal‑assembly compliance with Regulation 2018/858 across all models; document design margin.  
8. **Tesla Model Y wiring redesign (F296)** — evaluate impact on HV battery harness routing, ADAS sensor grounding, and OTA update paths.  
9. **Hyundai Ioniq 5 digital side mirrors (F266)** — monitor camera‑replace‑mirror homologation in EU/UK; track cybersecurity/OTA surface.  
10. **Open items (86)** — triage carry‑overs against new findings; close resolved, escalate stale.  

---

# Risk Brief — Compliance & Quality Watch  
**Profile:** Tesla Model Y 2021‑2025, Chevrolet Bolt EV 2019‑2023, Hyundai Ioniq 5 2022‑2025, Volkswagen ID.4 2021‑2025  
**Markets:** EU, UK, US

---

## Executive summary
- **Tesla Model Y FSD Beta cluster** — 5 complaints in 90 days (2.9× baseline) showing catastrophic lane‑keeping failures (guardrail/median/water departures, injuries, entrapment) on HW4 compute; no recall yet. Immediate OTA containment, HW4 power‑integrity audit, and NHTSA Early Warning Reporting required [S1].  
- **Chevrolet Bolt EV brake anti‑click washer fracture** — 3 complaints in 90 days (6× baseline) causing extreme wheel overheating (627 °F), steering wobble, harness melting, and fire risk; no recall yet. Issue TSB, audit harness routing, open ODI [S2].  
- **Chevrolet Bolt EV multi‑mode defect spike** — 3 complaints in 90 days (3× baseline) covering rear‑door entrapment, backup‑camera loss, and drivetrain washer fracture; one report cites existing door‑latch recall. Assess recall expansion for uncovered VINs [S3].  
- **Hyundai Ioniq 5 traction battery fire recall** (NHTSA 26V432000, 2026‑07‑02) — misaligned electrodes in 2023‑2024 cells; immediate quarantine and replacement of suspect cells [F220].  
- **Tesla Model Y rear‑view camera circuit‑board short** (NHTSA 25V002000, 2025‑01‑07) — loss of rear visibility on 2021‑2025 MY; halt software updates until fix deployed [F199].  
- **Volkswagen ID.4 door‑handle water ingress** (NHTSA 24V651000, 2024‑09‑04) — unexpected door opening on 2021‑2024 MY; inspect/replace handles [F239].  
- **Chevrolet Bolt EV HV battery remediation cascade** — multiple recalls (2020‑2024) for fire risk; latest recalls (24V481000, 24V812000) flag incorrect diagnostic‑software installation on previously repaired vehicles — validate installation fleet‑wide [F212, F213].

**VERDICT: FSD (Supervised) v14.2.2.4 exhibits catastrophic lane-keeping failures — veering into guardrails, medians, and a boat launch — causing multiple total-loss crashes with injuries and entrapment; HW4 computer degradation and possible EMI susceptibility compound the risk.**

**Failure Modes**  
- Perception/planning error: FSD misinterprets lane topology (merge zones, faded lines, boat ramps) as drivable path.  
- Latent HW4 fault: Prior low-voltage/VCFRONT/radar replacements culminate in total HW4 loss, suggesting compute-platform instability that may corrupt trajectory output.  
- EMI event: One report of area-wide ADAS/camera disablement near a rail facility, indicating external RF susceptibility.

**Safety Risk**  
High — 3/5 complaints involve high-speed departure into fixed objects or water with occupant injury/entrapment; one fire/smoke event; police reports and vehicle logs confirm FSD control at impact.

**Evidence Strength**  
Strong — 5 reports in 90 days (2.9× baseline), all 2025 MY, consistent FSD version, corroborated by sheriff/Tesla incident exports, physical vehicle preservation, and injury documentation.

**OEM Immediate Actions**  
1. Quarantine FSD v14.2.2.4 telemetry; pull HW4 crash kernels from all 3 totaled units.  
2. Run hardware-in-the-loop replay of merge/median/ramp scenarios; root-cause perception vs. planning vs. compute fault.  
3. Audit HW4 power-integrity (VCFRONT, 16 V bus) across fleet; issue containment OTA if compute brownout detected.  
4. Test EMI hardening at reported I-95 site; add RF-immunity acceptance criteria.  
5. Open NHTSA Early Warning Reporting; consider FSD suspension for affected VINs until patch validated.

**Verdict: Anti-click washer fracture causes brake drag → extreme wheel overheating (627°F), steering wobble, and harness thermal damage; loss-of-control and fire risk rising.**

**Failure mode:** The anti-rattle/anti-click washer (pad retention clip) fractures, allowing pad shift and continuous rotor drag. This generates extreme localized heat (627°F vs. <200°F other wheels), warping rotors, damaging wheel bearings (steering wobble), and melting adjacent wiring harnesses — triggering regenerative-braking alerts, propulsion loss, and RCM/airbag communication faults.

**Safety risk:** Sudden steering vibration and pull at speed → loss of control; bearing seizure or brake fade → crash; harness melting → fire and safety-system disablement (airbags, lighting, shift interlock).

**Evidence strength:** Strong — three independent reports, quantitative thermal data, recurrence after full brake replacement, dealer-confirmed broken washer + collateral damage, OEM blog documentation, and OnStar regenerative-braking alert. Spike 6× baseline.

**OEM immediate actions:** 1) Issue TSB for anti-click washer inspection/replacement on all 2017–2020 Bolts. 2) Audit harness routing near calipers for heat shielding. 3) Open safety investigation (ODI) for recall determination. 4) Notify NHTSA of regenerative-braking thermal cascade.

**No single common failure mode — three distinct safety defects: rear-door entrapment, backup-camera loss, and drivetrain "anti-click washer" fracture causing loss of acceleration/braking control.**

**Safety risks:**  
- Door latch: occupant entrapment in crash/fire (injury).  
- Reverse camera: backing collisions (crash).

**Evidence strength:** Moderate. One complaint cites an existing recall for same MY doors; one documents ≥3 dealer repair attempts; one provides dealer-confirmed broken washer + external technical article linking same design to prior-gen TSB.

2. Issue TSB/software fix for reverse-camera/infotainment; track warranty repeat repairs.  
3. Launch drivetrain investigation on anti-click washer durability; compare prior-gen TSB scope; consider field fix or recall if fracture causes loss of control.

**VERDICT: FSD (Supervised) v14.2.2.4 exhibits a systemic lane-departure failure mode — erroneous path planning causes vehicles to exit travel lanes into guardrails, medians/trees, and waterways — resulting in multiple total-loss crashes, injuries, fire/smoke, and occupant entrapment; evidence is strong (2.9× baseline, 5 reports with police data, preserved vehicles, confirmed FSD-active logs).**

**Failure Modes**  
- **Path-planning/geofence error**: FSD commands steering into physically impossible or prohibited corridors (merge guardrail, median crossover, boat launch).  
- **Sensor-fusion/map mismatch**: Yellow-line transitions, marina ramps, and rail-adjacent RF interference correlate with sudden ADAS disablement or wrong-turn decisions.  
- **Hardware cascade**: Low-voltage/VCFRONT/HW4 failures (Complaint 2) may degrade compute or sensor power, amplifying planner instability.

**Safety Risk**  
- **Crash**: 3/5 reports = total-loss collisions (guardrail, tree, submersion).  
- **Injury**: 2 children injured (fracture), driver near-drowning/entrapment.  
- **Fire**: Post-crash smoke/fire with door-lock entrapment (5 min).  
- **Secondary**: ADAS/camera disablement removes crash recording & fallback safety.

**Evidence Strength**  
- Statistical spike (5 vs 1.73 expected).  
- Police/sheriff reports, preserved vehicles, Tesla incident data exports confirming FSD active.  
- Consistent software version (2025.45.9.1 / FSD v14.2.2.4) across crash reports.

**Immediate OEM Actions**  
1. **Freeze OTA rollout** of v14.2.2.4; push hotfix restricting FSD on unmapped/ambiguous lanes (marinas, merge tapers, rail corridors).  
2. **Mandate data pull** from all 5 VINs + fleet telemetry for planner decision traces (steering torque, lane-probability maps, sensor confidence).  
3. **Root-cause HW4/low-voltage audit** — correlate compute brownouts with planner resets.  
4. **File 573.6 Defect Information Report** to NHTSA within 5 business days.  
5. **Owner comms**: advise “FSD Supervised = hands-on, eyes-on, immediate takeover ready” until fix validated.

**Verdict: Left-front caliper seizure/slide-pin corrosion causing persistent brake drag, extreme wheel overheating (627°F), steering wobble, and potential tire/brake-fluid failure; anti-rattle clip fracture and regenerative-braking harness damage are compounding factors.**

- **Common failure mode:** Caliper slide-pin corrosion or anti-rattle (“anti-click”) washer fracture locks the left-front brake in partial application. Heat soaks the wheel hub (627°F vs. <200°F others), warps the rotor, and induces violent steering shimmy. One owner saw recurrence three days after pad/rotor replacement. Dealer confirmed broken anti-click washer and collateral damage. Third report shows main-harness thermal damage (melted/charred wiring) triggering a Regenerative Braking System red alert—likely heat migration from the same corner.  
- **Safety risk:** Tire blowout, brake-fluid boil, wheel-bearing collapse, or fire; sudden steering wobble risks loss-of-control at speed.  
- **Evidence strength:** Moderate—three independent reports with quantitative temp data, repeat failure post-repair, dealer hardware confirmation, and telematics alert. No crashes/injuries yet.  
- **OEM actions:** 1) Issue TSB for left-front caliper slide-pin inspection, lubrication, and anti-rattle clip replacement on 2019 Bolt EV. 2) Audit warranty claims for LF brake overheating. 3) Reroute/main-harness shield near caliper heat zone. 4) Evaluate regenerative-braking fault strategy for thermal protection.

**Verdict: Three distinct defect trends (door latch entrapment, rear-camera loss, drivetrain "anti-click washer" failure) masquerade as a single statistical spike; each carries serious safety risk and warrants separate investigation.**

**Common failure modes & safety risks**  
- **Rear door latch**: Interior release mechanism fails → passenger entrapment, delayed egress in crash/fire (recall exists for 2019-2020).  
- **Rear camera/infotainment**: Persistent video loss after multiple dealer repairs → blind-zone backing, pedestrian/vehicle strike risk.  
- **Anti-click washer (drivetrain)**: Known prior-gen defect, same design → sudden loss of acceleration/braking control, component collateral damage; no warning lamps.

**Evidence strength**  
- Door latch: Owner cites existing recall for same vintage → **Strong** (pattern confirmed).  
- Camera: 3+ dealer visits, new-vehicle onset → **Moderate-Strong** (chronic, unresolved).  
- Washer: Dealer-confirmed broken part, external technical article, prior-gen TSB → **Strong** (root cause identified).

**OEM quality actions now**  
1. Split the spike into three component-specific investigations.  
2. Cross-check VINs against 2019-2020 door-latch recall; expand if same supplier/design.  
3. Issue TSB for camera software/hardware root cause; mandate fix before next sale.  
4. Fast-track drivetrain washer redesign; add dashboard alert; assess field population for proactive replacement.
